edges.description: The c.107-2A>G acceptor-site variant produces abnormal transcripts in the proband fibroblasts.
Abnormal transcripts accompany absent detectable protein; the relative contributions of RNA decay and protein degradation were not experimentally separated.
SURF1 deficiency compromises the efficient assembly of complex IV. Residual holoenzyme is detectable despite absent SURF1.
Lower assembled complex IV abundance accompanies reduced COX enzymatic activity in the proband.
Respiratory-chain dysfunction is associated with the neuropathy, but the route from COX deficiency to myelin injury is unresolved; Schwann-cell ATP failure was not measured.
Axonal loss accompanies the COX-deficient neuropathy; its timing relative to demyelination and cellular mechanism remain uncertain.
Reduced oxidative phosphorylation provides a biochemical rationale for elevated lactate, but the relevant tissue fluxes were not measured in these patients.
The biochemical defect is the measured phenotype.
Clinical and electrophysiologic manifestation of nerve myelin pathology.
Myelin dysfunction slows saltatory conduction.
Motor axonal injury can contribute to distal denervation and wasting; motor-unit loss was not separately quantified.
Sensory axonal dysfunction can contribute to lower-limb sensory loss; subtype-specific fiber loss was not measured.
Clinical biochemical finding described as lactic acidosis in the original series.
RT-PCR and sequencing identified exon skipping and cryptic acceptor usage.
edges.limitations: One CMT4K patient; fibroblasts rather than neurons or myelinating Schwann cells, with no isogenic correction. Tissue-level neuropathy mechanisms are not directly tested.

nodes.description: Preclinical SURF1 gene addition has been studied in the Leigh disease context. Lower-expression JeTI AAV9 constructs improve selected mouse COX readouts, but human CMT4K benefit has not been established by these experiments. The original CBh construct caused multi-tissue toxicity in rats; the revised design had no adverse histology in a small four-week rat experiment. This limited result does not establish long-term human safety. The reported exercise-lactate change with JeTI was not statistically significant against untreated knockout animals (p=0.0609).

nodes.description: The viable truncated-Surf1 model was studied in male mice aged 5–7 months for heart and skeletal-muscle energetics. COX activity fell 71% in heart and 53% in muscle, but isolated mitochondrial ATP production was not significantly reduced. Mitochondrial biogenesis markers increased in both tissues; UPRmt markers increased principally in muscle and Nrf2/HO-1 in heart. Basal and exercise lactate increased and endurance declined. These adaptations do not demonstrate a compensatory mechanism in human CMT4K nerve.
